title: When Is Free Relief Allowed for Abnormal Course Conditions?
question: In which of these situations are you allowed to take free relief for an abnormal course condition?

choices.text: Your ball is lying in temporary water
Your stance would be on a mole hill
You are distracted by the sight of a path a long way off
Your swing is physically interfered with by an immovable obstruction

explanation: Free relief is allowed if your play is physically interfered with by temporary water, an animal hole, or an immovable obstruction. Mere distraction, such as seeing a path in the distance, does not qualify.

juniorVersion.title: When Can You Move Your Ball for Free Because Something Is in the Way?
juniorVersion.question: Which of these times can you pick up and drop your ball somewhere better because something on the course is stopping your shot?

choices.text: Your ball is sitting in a big puddle.
You have to stand on a mole hill to hit your ball.
You see a path far away and it makes you lose focus.
A bench that can’t be moved is blocking your swing.

juniorVersion.explanation: You can move your ball for free if it is sitting in a puddle, you have to stand on a mole hill, or if something big that you can't move (like a bench or sprinkler) is in your way when you try to play your shot. Just seeing something that distracts you, like a path far away, does not count.

vocabulary.simpleMeaning: Something on the course, like a bench or a big sign, that you can’t move.
A puddle made by lots of rain that is not always there.
A small hill of dirt made by a mole.
You are allowed to move your ball somewhere better without a penalty.

juniorVersion.teachingTip: Show kids real examples on the course, like puddles, animal holes, and things that can't be moved. Let them practise finding the nearest place to drop a ball for free relief.
likelyMisconceptions: Children might think they get free relief just because something looks odd or they are distracted.
Kids may not know the difference between things they can move, like a rake, and things they cannot, like a sprinkler.
